summary: Risk assessment for issue #1765 — exposing egg agent capabilities to sandbox agents as in-process MCP tools (claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server + @tool decorators wired into shared/egg_agent/client.py::run_agent_async). Iteration 1 ships ~15 verbs covering BRC + HITL + phase-context core, naming by semantic verb (mcp__sdlc__*, mcp__brc__*, mcp__phase__*). Existing sandbox/bin/egg-* CLIs are kept indefinitely for humans/tests/recovery scripts; the MCP layer is additive. Identified 12 risks across security, reliability, performance, compatibility, operability, rollout, and supply chain. Two are HIGH (blocking-IO/sys.exit in shared CLI handlers; SDK version drift), three are MEDIUM, the rest are LOW. None are blocking the plan; all have concrete mitigations and most should be encoded as plan-task acceptance criteria.

scope_assumed.decision_1_mechanism: Hybrid D + prompt nudge: in-process SDK MCP server via create_sdk_mcp_server + @tool, wired into shared/egg_agent/client.py::run_agent_async, plus a short system-prompt paragraph pointing agents at the mcp__* tools
scope_assumed.decision_2_handler_derivation: Hybrid: auto-derive skeleton from existing CLI/argparse signatures, allow per-tool overrides for descriptions/schemas
scope_assumed.decision_3_harness_coverage: claude_agent_sdk harness only for iteration 1; defer EGG_HARNESS=egg parallel registration
scope_assumed.decision_4_cli_retention: Keep sandbox/bin/egg-* CLIs indefinitely; MCP tools are purely additive for agents
scope_assumed.decision_7_naming: Semantic verbs grouped by function (mcp__sdlc__register_open_question, mcp__brc__propose, mcp__phase__get_context)
scope_assumed.decision_8_iteration1_scope: BRC + HITL + phase-context core (~15 verbs): brc_propose/ack/nack/confirm/get_state/list_blocking; hitl_register_decision/request_feedback/check_answers; phase_get_context/get_assigned_tasks; progress_emit/signal_error/heartbeat; task_complete

risks.title: Reusing sync CLI handler functions inside @tool-decorated async functions blocks the SDK event loop and may sys.exit() the agent
evidence: sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py:239-291 — make_gateway_request() uses urllib.request.urlopen with timeout=30s (blocking sync I/O); on HTTPError/URLError/TimeoutError it calls sys.exit(1) (lines 284, 288, 291).
sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py:736-833 — cmd_add_decision (and siblings cmd_add_commit, cmd_complete_task, cmd_add_feedback) is sync, prints to stdout via print(), calls make_gateway_request().

claude_agent_sdk @tool decorator expects an async callable returning a content dict (claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py:185-190). Synchronous blocking I/O inside an async tool handler stalls the agent's whole asyncio loop until urlopen returns.
A sys.exit() inside an in-process tool handler kills the agent's Python interpreter, which the orchestrator will then see as an agent crash (not a tool error).
risks.impact: Agent freezes for 30s during gateway slowness; on transient gateway error the agent dies entirely instead of receiving a tool-result error it could recover from. Affects every MCP tool that wraps a contract_cli function.
mitigation: MANDATORY: in the @tool handler, wrap any blocking handler in asyncio.to_thread(...) (or refactor to httpx.AsyncClient).

MANDATORY: refactor make_gateway_request (or create a parallel async-friendly variant) so HTTP errors raise an exception instead of sys.exit(1). The exception is caught in the @tool handler and returned as a structured tool result {content:[...], is_error: true}.
Acceptance criterion for plan: 'No @tool handler may call a function that calls sys.exit on the failure path; no @tool handler may perform blocking I/O on the asyncio loop.'
Add a smoke test that triggers a gateway 5xx and asserts the agent receives a tool-error result (not a process exit).
risks.rollback_plan: Set MCP server config tools=[] or unset mcp_servers in ClaudeAgentOptions; agents transparently fall back to Bash + sandbox/bin/egg-* (since the CLIs are retained per decision-4).

risks.title: claude-agent-sdk version is unpinned at build time; if a future version changes create_sdk_mcp_server / @tool semantics, every sandbox image silently breaks
evidence: sandbox/Dockerfile:216-228 — ARG CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION=latest; the egg build script normally passes a specific version, but the manual fallback installs 'latest'.
sandbox/pyproject.toml:9 — dependency declared as bare 'claude-agent-sdk' (no version constraint).

Currently shipping claude-agent-sdk==0.1.65 (verified at /usr/local/lib/python3.13/dist-packages/claude_agent_sdk; create_sdk_mcp_server confirmed at __init__.py:302). 0.1.x is pre-1.0 with no API-stability guarantees.
shared/egg_agent/client.py:148-155 already gracefully handles ImportError (returns AgentResult with error message), but does NOT guard against SDK semantic changes.
risks.impact: A future SDK release (e.g. 0.2.x) can change @tool's argument-shape contract or McpSdkServerConfig; agents start crashing on import or on first tool call. Especially risky because the in-process MCP path is novel surface relative to the existing query() call.
mitigation: Pin claude-agent-sdk to >=0.1.65,<0.2 in sandbox/pyproject.toml and pass that exact version to the Docker build via the egg script (the script already supports this).
Add a build-time smoke test (one-shot) that creates an SDK MCP server with a no-op tool and asserts options.mcp_servers accepts McpSdkServerConfig — fails the image build on regression.
Document the SDK version coupling in sandbox/agent-config/rules/environment.md (or a new mcp-tools.md) so the next person bumping the SDK knows to re-validate.
Track SDK release notes in the repo with each bump; gate bumps on a pipeline run that exercises every MCP tool registered.
risks.rollback_plan: Roll the sandbox image back to a pinned prior tag (egg sandbox image is tagged per build); the shell CLIs still work, so agents continue functioning at reduced ergonomics until the SDK is downgraded.

risks.title: permission_mode=bypassPermissions + can_use_tool callback only checks Write/Edit/NotebookEdit — custom MCP verbs (e.g. mcp__sdlc__register_open_question) bypass file-write boundaries entirely
evidence: shared/egg_agent/client.py:194 — permission_mode='bypassPermissions' is hardcoded.

shared/egg_agent/client.py:163-191 — can_use_tool callback dispatches to check_file_write_permission, which (per shared/egg_agent/tool_interceptor.py) only matches Write/Edit/NotebookEdit by tool_name; MCP-prefixed names like mcp__sdlc__... will not match.
Sandbox-side @tool handlers will run with the caller agent's full file-system access via permission_mode='bypassPermissions'.

Gateway-side authz is the actual trust boundary (BearerToken EGG_SESSION_TOKEN); but if a handler chooses to operate on files locally instead of calling the gateway (e.g. a future tool that writes to .egg-state/), it bypasses both layers.
risks.impact: A bug or misuse in a future MCP tool handler that touches the filesystem could cross role boundaries (e.g. risk_analyst writing into src/) without the can_use_tool callback intercepting. Iteration 1's ~15 verbs are all gateway-mediated, so blast radius is small TODAY but grows as the surface expands.
mitigation: Acceptance criterion for plan: 'Iteration-1 MCP handlers MUST NOT perform direct filesystem writes; all state mutations route through the gateway, which enforces role-based authz.'

Update shared/egg_agent/tool_interceptor.py:check_file_write_permission to ALSO match the mcp__* prefix (defensive, future-proofing) — flag any MCP tool whose name pattern indicates write semantics for explicit role checks.
Add a unit test that asserts every @tool decorator name is in an allow-list reviewed by hand; new tools go through code review.

Consider populating allowed_tools=[...] in ClaudeAgentOptions to explicitly enumerate the agent-visible MCP tools per role (the SDK supports this — see types.py around ClaudeAgentOptions). Iteration 1 may not need this granularity but it's the natural place to add it later.
risks.rollback_plan: Remove the offending @tool from the registered tools list; redeploy. No data loss because gateway-side authz is the actual trust boundary.

risks.title: System-prompt 'use mcp__* tools' nudge has a recurring per-turn token cost AND is a hand-maintained string that can drift from the actual tool surface
evidence: decision-1 resolution mandates a 'short system-prompt paragraph pointing agents at the mcp__* tools'.
shared/egg_agent/client.py:209-211 — system_prompt is set per-call: options.system_prompt = system_prompt.
claude-agent-sdk renders the system_prompt on every turn (no incremental caching of the prompt within a single query call once the model context resets).
Anthropic prompt cache TTL is 5 minutes — a per-spawn nudge is amortized cheaply for a continuous run but recomputed on every fresh agent spawn.
Hand-maintained tool-list strings drift: the analysis itself (.egg-state/drafts/1765-analysis.md:541-548) lists indicative names that may diverge from final implementation.
risks.impact: Each agent spawn pays an extra ~150-300 tokens per turn for the nudge; across thousands of agent runs/month this is real but bounded. More worrying: if the nudge text references a tool name that gets renamed during implementation, the nudge silently misleads the agent and we lose the bootstrap benefit it was added to provide.
mitigation: Generate the prompt nudge from the same registry of @tool definitions that feeds create_sdk_mcp_server (single source of truth); never hand-author the tool-name list inside the prompt.

Cap the nudge at <=200 tokens (decision-1 already says 'short paragraph'); if the surface ever needs more guidance, that's a signal to put it in CLAUDE.md (which is read once at session init) instead of the per-turn system_prompt.
Acceptance criterion for plan: 'Tool names referenced in the system-prompt nudge MUST be derived programmatically from the @tool registry, not duplicated as a string literal.'
Add a CI test asserting the prompt-nudge text matches the registered tool names exactly.
risks.rollback_plan: Drop the nudge from the system prompt; tools still work via SDK's native tool discovery, just with the known 'agents default to Bash' regression risk that the nudge was added to mitigate.

risks.title: Existing CLI handlers print results to stdout; called in-process, that output is lost — the @tool handler returns an empty content block instead of the meaningful response
evidence: sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py:818-833 — cmd_add_decision prints the JSON response with print(json.dumps(...)); the function returns int (exit code), not the JSON.
Same pattern in cmd_add_commit (lines 396-440), cmd_complete_task (lines 484-558), cmd_add_feedback (lines 1294-1396): print on stdout, return int.

claude_agent_sdk @tool's contract is to return {content: [{type:'text', text:'...'}]} (per the docstring example at claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py:329-331). Print-to-stdout output never reaches that content.

decision-2 (handler derivation) explicitly says 'auto-derive skeleton from existing CLI/argparse signatures' — that auto-derivation will produce wrappers that call the print-emitting functions directly.
risks.impact: MCP tools wired to existing CLI functions will return empty/uninformative content blocks even when they succeed. Agents see ambiguous tool results and either retry or proceed blind, defeating the discoverability goal.
mitigation: MANDATORY: the implement-phase plan must split each contract_cli.cmd_* function into a pure logic core (returns dict) + a thin print-and-exit wrapper (used by the CLI). The MCP @tool handler calls the core; the CLI keeps its current contract.
Acceptance criterion for plan: 'Every shared handler invoked by a @tool MUST return its payload as a Python data structure (dict/list); printing/logging is the wrapper''s responsibility.'
Add unit tests that call each shared handler directly and assert the returned structure (not stdout).
Add an integration test that calls the @tool through the SDK and asserts the returned content is non-empty and reflects the operation.
risks.rollback_plan: If the refactor proves too invasive in one PR, fall back to subprocess invocation inside the @tool handler (loses the in-process benefit but preserves the structured-return contract). Either way, the shell CLIs continue to work for human/test consumers.

risks.title: Existing orchestrator MCP server tools and new sandbox MCP tools share the mcp__ prefix; agents (or human operators reading checkpoint logs) may conflate them
evidence: orchestrator/mcp_server.py runs FastMCP on port 9850 with tools defined in orchestrator/mcp_tools.py (PIPELINE_TOOLS list): submit_task, run_agent_task, babysit_pr, get_status, cancel_task, get_consensus_status, restart_phase, etc.
These are exposed to host-side Claude Code only; sandbox agents do NOT receive them as MCP tools (they're not in the sandbox agent's mcp_servers config).

Both surfaces will use the mcp__<server>__<tool> naming convention (SDK convention). Distinct server names (e.g. mcp__sdlc__* vs no prefix in orchestrator's case) prevent name collision in the protocol.
Risk is human/cognitive (checkpoint browser, log search) not technical.
risks.impact: Operators reading a checkpoint may confuse a sandbox-side mcp__sdlc__register_open_question call with an orchestrator-side tool. No security risk because the two surfaces are physically separated (different processes, different transports).
mitigation: Document the two MCP surfaces clearly in CLAUDE.md (or a new docs/reference/mcp-surfaces.md): one is host-side / orchestrator-managed, the other is sandbox-in-process. Name them distinctly.
Pick semantic-verb server names for sandbox tools (mcp__sdlc__, mcp__brc__, mcp__phase__) that are obviously not orchestrator-side (which has mcp__egg__ or similar host-facing names).
Update sandbox/agent-config/rules/orchestrator.md or a new rules file to explicitly list the sandbox MCP tools and clarify they are NOT the orchestrator MCP tools.
risks.rollback_plan: Rename to remove ambiguity; this is a string-rename PR, no data migration.

risks.title: Iteration 1 must work identically in public AND private network modes (AC requirement); in-process MCP avoids egress but tools that wrap CLIs still call the gateway over intra-cluster HTTP
evidence: Acceptance criterion: 'The chosen solution works in both public and private network modes' (issue #1765).
sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py:289-290 — make_gateway_request connects via urllib.request.urlopen to the gateway URL (intra-cluster Service); no proxy involvement, works identically in both modes.

shared/egg_agent/client.py:160-161 — disallowed_tools=['WebFetch', 'WebSearch'] in private mode; this list is checked by name only and will NOT block mcp__* tools that accidentally make external HTTP calls.
Iteration-1 verbs (BRC, HITL, phase context) are all gateway-mediated and intra-cluster; no external egress needed.
risks.impact: If iteration 2 (or a misinterpreted iteration-1 spec) adds a tool that makes an external HTTP call (e.g. a future github-issue-fetch tool), it will silently work in public mode and fail in private mode — discovered late.
mitigation: Acceptance criterion for plan: 'Iteration-1 @tool handlers MUST NOT make any external HTTP request; all I/O routes via the gateway URL or filesystem.'
Add a CI test that exercises every registered @tool in private-mode-equivalent network conditions (no external egress) and asserts they all succeed.
When iteration 2 adds tools with potential external dependencies, gate them on a private_mode check inside the handler (return a structured 'unavailable in private mode' error).
risks.rollback_plan: Network-mode-incompatible tools can be removed from the iteration-1 registry without affecting other tools (the registry is a list passed to create_sdk_mcp_server).

risks.title: decision-3 ships only for the claude_agent_sdk harness; agents running EGG_HARNESS=egg get NO MCP tools and continue paying the discoverability cost — divergent UX between harnesses
evidence: shared/egg_agent/client.py:99-127 — if EGG_HARNESS=egg, code routes to egg_harness_integration with its own ToolRegistry (shared/egg_harness/tools/) and never touches ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers.

decision-3 resolution explicitly defers parallel registration ('claude_agent_sdk harness only for iteration 1; defer parallel registration for experimental EGG_HARNESS=egg until that harness graduates').
EGG_HARNESS=egg is opt-in and currently used only for parity validation (scripts/validate_harness_parity.py exists but no production rollout).
risks.impact: Anyone explicitly opting into EGG_HARNESS=egg sees the same 'argparse archaeology' pain that issue #1765 documents. Acceptable for experimental traffic; unacceptable if egg harness graduates while iteration 1 hasn't been ported.
mitigation: Document the limitation prominently in shared/egg_harness/README.md (or analogous): 'MCP agent tools are SDK-harness-only; egg-harness agents fall back to Bash + sandbox/bin/.'
When/if the egg harness graduates from experimental, file a follow-up issue (similar to #1917 for iteration-2 verbs) to add parallel registration via shared/egg_harness/tools/.

Acceptance criterion for plan: 'The handler functions written for iteration 1 MUST be reusable from a future shared/egg_harness/tools/ wrapper without refactor (i.e. handlers accept a context object, not specifically an SDK ToolContext).'
risks.rollback_plan: N/A — feature is additive only on the SDK harness; egg harness is unaffected.

risks.title: MCP tool calls show up in the checkpoint stream as a new event type the existing browser/search tools may not handle gracefully
evidence: Today, agent calls to egg-* CLIs appear as Bash tool_use blocks in the checkpoint store (confirmed by egg-checkpoint browse output across recent pipelines).
claude_agent_sdk routes mcp__* tools through the same tool_use stream but with a different tool_name; the SDK is documented to surface them as first-class.
egg-checkpoint search currently filters by tool_name; users searching for 'egg-contract' to find decision-creation events would miss mcp__sdlc__register_open_question.
Feedback Q6 in the analysis explicitly raises this: 'should MCP tool calls generate distinct log events / checkpoints separate from the SDK''s built-in tool_use stream?'
risks.impact: Existing operator tooling and dashboards that grep for egg-contract / egg-orch invocations in checkpoints will under-count agent activity once MCP tools land. Forensic value of historical checkpoints is degraded until search queries are updated.
mitigation: Acceptance criterion for plan: 'egg-checkpoint search must support a query that matches both the legacy Bash-CLI form and the new mcp__* form for the same logical operation. At minimum, document the equivalence in docs/reference/checkpoint-cli.md.'
Optional: add a mapping table in shared/egg_contracts/checkpoint_cli.py (e.g. egg-contract add-decision <-> mcp__sdlc__register_open_question) consulted by the search subcommand.
Update the checkpoint-browser doc to call out the rename for operators and link to the mapping.
risks.rollback_plan: Search-side change is independent of the MCP rollout; even if not done at iteration-1, operators can grep for both names. Low urgency.

risks.title: Unit tests of run_agent_async will need to mock create_sdk_mcp_server / @tool registrations; existing test patterns may not cover the new path
evidence: tests/shared/egg_agent/test_client.py exists but currently mocks only the SDK query() function; no precedent for asserting mcp_servers-shaped options.
shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_client.py covers the egg harness path with custom mocks for AgentLoop / ToolRegistry — it will not exercise the SDK MCP path.
orchestrator/tests/test_mcp_tools.py mocks FastMCP but is for the orchestrator-side server (different surface).
risks.impact: Without test coverage of the new mcp_servers wiring, a regression in the SDK or in the @tool registration goes undetected until production. Manageable but adds tester workload.
mitigation: Plan task: 'Add tests/shared/egg_agent/test_client_mcp.py that asserts ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers contains an entry for each registered server, that handler dispatch works through the SDK''s in-process MCP machinery, and that a tool error is surfaced as a tool_result with is_error=true (not as an agent crash).'
Add a smoke test that boots a minimal in-process MCP server with a no-op @tool and asserts the SDK accepts it (catches SDK-version regressions per R2).
Use the SDK's documented testing patterns (claude_agent_sdk has examples in its test fixtures); avoid hand-rolling MCP protocol mocks.
risks.rollback_plan: N/A — test gap, not a runtime issue. Mitigated by writing tests alongside the implementation.

risks.title: Iteration 1 lands MCP tools for ALL sandbox agents (every role) at once; if a single role-specific handler regresses, every agent of that role is affected
evidence: shared/egg_agent/client.py is the single entry point for ALL sandbox agents regardless of role (refiner, architect, coder, tester, reviewer_*, etc.).
The mcp_servers parameter is set per-call; once added, every agent invocation receives the registered tools.
decision-1 mandates wiring into client.py — there is no per-role gate today.
Feedback Q8 in the analysis raises this: 'should the MCP tool surface be enabled for all roles simultaneously, or gated behind a feature flag (EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true) during a burn-in window?'
risks.impact: A bug in mcp__brc__propose blocks every producer agent across every pipeline. Blast radius is large and recovery is 'wait for the next image build', not 'restart the offending pod'.
mitigation: Acceptance criterion for plan: 'The MCP-server registration in shared/egg_agent/client.py MUST be gated behind an env var EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true (default opt-IN, but kill-switch available). Operators can disable mcp_servers with a single env edit on the spawner without rebuilding the image.'
Roll out with metrics: track per-pipeline tool-call counts and Bash-fallback rates in checkpoint logs for the first week.
Document the kill-switch in docs/reference/orchestrator-cli.md and in the agent-recovery runbook so on-call can disable quickly.
When the kill-switch fires, agents transparently fall back to Bash + sandbox/bin/ (decision-4 retains the CLIs).
risks.rollback_plan: Set EGG_MCP_TOOLS=false on the spawner ConfigMap, restart the spawner; new agent pods use Bash. No data migration. Existing in-flight pipelines continue with their original tool surface (env is read at spawn).

risks.title: @tool handlers run in the agent's own Python process and can read/mutate any module-level state; a handler that accidentally caches per-pipeline data leaks across agent invocations within the same container
evidence: Sandbox containers spawn ONE Python process per agent (per orchestrator/kubernetes_spawner.py); each container handles ONE agent invocation, then exits.
BUT: if a future optimization reuses containers across invocations (or a developer adds module-level caching during the iteration-1 implementation), shared state becomes visible across pipelines.

The proposed mcp__phase__get_context handler in decision-8 reads EGG_PIPELINE_ID / EGG_AGENT_ROLE from os.environ — if cached at module-load instead of read on each call, a reused container serves stale context.
risks.impact: Today's one-process-per-agent model makes this a non-issue; the risk surfaces only if container reuse is ever introduced (#1873/#1875 already fight container lifecycle bugs; this becomes a risk multiplier).
mitigation: Acceptance criterion for plan: 'No @tool handler may cache pipeline-scoped state in module-level globals; all per-call context (EGG_PIPELINE_ID, EGG_AGENT_ROLE, cwd) must be read from os.environ inside the handler call, not at import time.'
Add a unit test that imports the tools module twice and asserts no module-level state has been populated by mere import.
Document the constraint in the new sandbox/egg_agent_tools/ package's README so future contributors know the rule.
risks.rollback_plan: If a leak is found in production, set EGG_MCP_TOOLS=false (R11 kill-switch) and ship a fix in the next image.

areas_for_human_review.question: Confirm operators want EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true as the default (opt-out via flag) vs. opt-in (default false during a burn-in week). Feedback Q8 in the analysis raised this; no resolution captured in HITL decisions.

Is it acceptable for the implement-phase PR to refactor sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py to split logic from print/exit (the proper fix), or should it be deferred behind a subprocess wrapper (faster ship, loses in-process benefit)? Plan needs a clear directive — drives task scoping.

Should iteration 1 already populate ClaudeAgentOptions.allowed_tools per role (e.g. risk_analyst sees mcp__phase__*, mcp__brc__*, mcp__sdlc__* but not mcp__progress__heartbeat) or is the whole iteration-1 set visible to every role? Affects authz-by-construction story.

Decision-2 picked 'hybrid: auto-derive skeleton, allow per-tool overrides' but did not commit to a CI mechanism. Should plan add a CI test that asserts every @tool's argument schema matches a single shared handler signature? (Recommended yes — closes the drift door cleanly.)

areas_for_human_review.topic: Output shape for diagnostic tools (Feedback Q4)
areas_for_human_review.question: brc_get_state and similar tools naturally return JSON. Plan should pick: verbatim JSON, compact text summary, or both (multi-block). Affects token cost per tool call. Not blocking but should be settled before implementation.

non_risks_explicitly_considered.rationale: In-process MCP has no network surface; the gateway calls the existing CLIs already make work in both modes via intra-cluster Service URL. Decision-1 specifically picked Option D over C to avoid this risk. Mentioned as R7 in a forward-looking sense only.

non_risks_explicitly_considered.topic: Authn/authz to a separate MCP server
non_risks_explicitly_considered.rationale: Option C (separate orchestrator-hosted MCP server with bearer auth) was NOT chosen; the in-process Option D inherits the agent's existing trust boundary. Feedback Q5 (token lifecycle) is moot for this iteration.

non_risks_explicitly_considered.topic: MCP server inside the sandbox container as a daemon
non_risks_explicitly_considered.rationale: Explicitly ruled out by the issue ('Not on the table'). Not assessed.
decision-4 explicitly retains them indefinitely; humans, tests, entrypoint scripts, and bash recovery wrappers depend on them. No migration risk.

external_research_summary.rationale: The change is internal: it introduces in-process Python tools to a Python codebase, depends on an already-installed library (claude-agent-sdk 0.1.65, verified in the running container), and does not bring in new third-party packages. claude-agent-sdk is an Anthropic-published SDK with no known CVEs at the pinned version; the create_sdk_mcp_server / @tool / McpSdkServerConfig surface is documented in the installed SDK source (claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py:185-515, types.py:574-622). No external WebSearch/WebFetch was needed to assess these risks.

recommended_plan_acceptance_criteria: AC: No @tool handler may call sys.exit on the failure path; failures must propagate as exceptions captured by the handler and returned as {is_error: true, content: [...]} (R1).
AC: No @tool handler may perform blocking I/O on the asyncio event loop; sync handler functions must be invoked via asyncio.to_thread() or refactored to async (R1).
AC: Every shared handler invoked by a @tool MUST return its payload as a Python data structure; printing/logging is the responsibility of the CLI wrapper (R5).
AC: Tool names referenced in the system-prompt nudge MUST be derived programmatically from the @tool registry, not duplicated as a string literal (R4).
AC: The MCP-server registration in shared/egg_agent/client.py MUST be gated behind EGG_MCP_TOOLS env var so operators can kill-switch without rebuilding the image (R11).
AC: claude-agent-sdk MUST be pinned to a compatible version range (>=0.1.65,<0.2) in sandbox/pyproject.toml and the sandbox image build script (R2).
AC: Iteration-1 @tool handlers MUST NOT perform direct filesystem writes; all state mutations route via the gateway (R3).
AC: Iteration-1 @tool handlers MUST NOT make external HTTP requests; only intra-cluster gateway calls and filesystem reads are permitted (R7).
AC: The handler functions written for iteration 1 MUST be reusable from a future shared/egg_harness/tools/ wrapper without refactor (R8).
AC: No @tool handler may cache pipeline-scoped state in module-level globals; per-call context must be read inside the handler (R12).
AC: Tests in tests/shared/egg_agent/ MUST cover (a) mcp_servers wiring, (b) tool-error surfacing as tool_result, (c) a smoke test that catches SDK-version regression on import (R2, R10).

overall_assessment.go_no_go: GO with mitigations encoded as plan-task acceptance criteria
overall_assessment.summary: The chosen approach (in-process SDK MCP server) is architecturally clean and avoids the entire class of network/auth risks that drove Option C off the table. The non-trivial risks (R1 blocking-IO/sys.exit, R5 stdout-print-loses-output) are rooted in the SHARED handler functions' current sync+CLI design — they require a small refactor in sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py before the MCP wrappers can call them safely. R2 (SDK version pinning) is a one-line discipline fix. R3 (permission scope) and R4 (prompt nudge drift) are best handled as forward-looking acceptance criteria the implementer follows. R11 (kill-switch) is essential operational hygiene given the broad rollout. None of the risks block the plan; all have concrete mitigations the plan can encode as acceptance criteria for the implement phase.
